captions.detailed: This 3D model represents a highly detailed bicycle front-end assembly, featuring a fork and drop handlebars. The central support is a blue cylindrical head tube stub enclosing a silver steerer tube. Above this, a black stem clamps onto a curved drop-style handlebar equipped with dual brake levers and thin, arched cable housings. Below, the steering column terminates in a rectangular fork crown holding two rigid, downward-extending fork blades with wheel-mounting dropouts. The handlebars, stem, and fork are designed to rotate together as a single unit relative to the fixed head tube stub.
captions.instruction: Create a detailed 3D model of a bicycle front-end subassembly. The model must include a blue cylindrical head tube, a silver steerer tube, a black rectangular fork crown with two downward-extending rigid fork blades, a matching black stem, and curved drop handlebars equipped with brake levers and cable arcs. Ensure the steering assembly (handlebars, stem, and fork) is articulated to rotate realistically about the vertical steerer axis.
captions.factory: The assembly is constructed using multiple parts and a revolute joint. First, a fixed head tube stub is created with a blue cylinder and a central silver steerer shaft. Next, the steerable assembly is modeled as a child part containing the fork crown (a rectangular box), the fork blades (modeled with swept profiles or cylinders), the stem clamp, the drop handlebars (swept along a curved path), and the brake lever hardware. Finally, a revolute articulation is defined along the vertical Z-axis, connecting the fixed head tube to the rotating fork and handlebar assembly.
